A. Output: 
Fallback-path connector and contract integration across the public `cardano-lightning-relay`, `cardano-lightning-client`, and `lightning-liquidity-manager` repositories. For MS3 we used the fallback path defined in the milestone: Bitcoin RPC + Lightning channel flow on the relay side, and locked-funds coordination with the Liquidity Manager contract on the Cardano side, without Cardinal mint/burn. The fallback path was chosen because Cardinal did not provide usable developer tooling for implementation during this milestone window: only high-level public specifications were available, and no maintained SDK or integration-ready tooling was available to build against.

ms.report:
A. Output: 
A public open source demo frontend and relay-backed bridge flow were delivered for both required directions: BTC via Lightning to wrapped BTC on Cardano Preprod, and wrapped BTC on Cardano Preprod to BTC via Lightning. The demo frontend is deployed at https://cardano-ln.perun.network and connects to the public Connector API at http://cardano-ln.perun.network:30305. The frontend supports onramp requests, Lightning invoice display, payment status tracking, offramp requests, cBTC deposit confirmation, progress views, transaction history, pool information, and metrics.
Acceptance criteria: 
The public demo URL, Connector base URL, and Preprod script address are published. The implementation demonstrates 10 Lightning-to-Cardano payments and 10 Cardano-to-Lightning payments on Bitcoin Signet and Cardano Preprod. The structured evidence records payment hashes, Lightning preimages, Cardano transaction hashes, amounts, and pool state for all 20 swaps. The Preprod script address used in the evidence run is `addr_test1wqf2s47jetde0ne0n0u9vfrm04q363n5ycnzyupen5j20hqple0j8`; the cBTC policy ID is `c1474e383d24055c747cdfbddb33223276e675bab82ba8969ac13a36`; the asset name is `63425443`; and the Lightning channel ID is `0f7f1ae048c43a6cffb8298f1984324089307548b9df2b353d3831eb96d052eb`.
